collectionDialog.title: Import Steam Workshop Collection
collectionDialog.description: Paste a collection URL to add all its mods to your server config at once
collectionDialog.urlHelp: A Collection is a curated list of multiple mods bundled together by its creator. Paste the collection's own URL or numeric ID here — a single mod's Workshop page won't work. To add just one mod, use Add Mod instead.
collectionDialog.noModsFound: No mods found in this collection. Check the URL and try again.
collectionDialog.openWorkshopAria: Open workshop page (opens in new tab)

addModDialog.title: Add Workshop Mod
addModDialog.descPrefix: Paste a Steam Workshop URL or ID — or
addModDialog.inputPlaceholder: Paste Workshop URL or enter ID...
addModDialog.alreadyAdded: Workshop ID is already in your server config
addModDialog.modIdsHelp: A Workshop item can register more than one internal Mod ID — the folder name declared in its mod.info, not the Workshop's own numeric ID. Only what's selected here gets added to the server config; leave one out and that part of the mod silently won't load.
addModDialog.preSelectedHint: New IDs are pre-selected automatically. Open Review IDs to manually adjust selection.
addModDialog.unconventionalStructure: This mod may use an unconventional structure
addModDialog.addAndSyncLater: Add the Workshop ID and sync after server downloads it

restartSettingsDialog.title: Auto-Restart Settings
restartSettingsDialog.description: Configure how the server restarts when mod updates are detected
restartSettingsDialog.warningTimeHint: How long to wait before restarting after detecting updates
restartSettingsDialog.delayIfPlayersHint: Wait for all players to leave before restarting
restartSettingsDialog.maxDelayHint: Force restart after this time even if players are online

installedTab.showDisabledTooltip: Mods downloaded to disk but not enabled in the server INI
installedTab.collectionSyncTooltip: Sync tracked mods → Steam Workshop collection
installedTab.noResultsDesc: Try a different search term, or clear the filter.

installedTab.emptyDesc: The panel watches tracked mods for Workshop updates, surfaces conflicts, and lets you reorder load order with one click.
installedTab.syncFromServerDesc: Imports the WorkshopItems and Mods= lines from your active server config.
installedTab.importCollectionDesc: Paste a Steam Workshop collection URL to add every mod in it at once.
installedTab.addSingleModDesc: Track a specific mod by its Workshop ID or full URL.
installedTab.trackingMetadataOnly: Tracking is metadata only — mods are downloaded by your server, not the panel.

disabledPanel.title: Disabled mods on disk
disabledPanel.subtitle: — downloaded but not loaded by the server
disabledPanel.empty: No disabled mods. Everything in the workshop folder is enabled in the server INI.
disabledPanel.scanFailedDesc: The workshop folder scan failed. Try refreshing again.

serverConfigTab.workshopItemsNoModIds: {{count}} workshop items configured but no mod IDs. Run "Sync Mod IDs" after downloading mods.
serverConfigTab.deduplicateEndpointUnavailable: Failed to deduplicate — server endpoint not available
serverConfigTab.notConfiguredHint: Start the server once — it will create the INI file automatically.

activeMods.idsEnabledTooltip: {{enabled}} of {{total}} mod IDs are currently enabled. "Mod IDs" are the internal names PZ loads — a single Workshop item can ship several IDs (variants, add-on packs, etc.).
activeMods.needsAttentionTooltip: Show only workshop items with a confirmed variant clash, a missing required mod ID, or a duplicate internal ID.
activeMods.multiIdShowingTooltip: Showing only workshop items with more than one mod ID. These are usually variants where only some should be enabled together.
activeMods.multiIdHint: Show only workshop items with multiple mod IDs (usually variants — only enable the ones you want).
activeMods.missingDepTooltip: At least one enabled mod requires another mod that isn't enabled. See the Conflicts tab → Missing Dependencies.
activeMods.duplicateIdTooltip: Multiple workshop items declare the same internal mod ID. Only one will load — review the Conflicts tab.
activeMods.helpText: This is what the server config actually loads. A Workshop item can ship several internal mod IDs — add-ons, variants, and shared libraries. Enabled IDs are green; those are the ones Project Zomboid loads. Select a row to toggle its IDs in the panel on the right.
activeMods.densityCompactTooltip: One line per Workshop item. Toggle individual mod IDs in the panel on the right.
activeMods.densityDetailedTooltip: Show every mod ID as a clickable chip inside each row.
activeMods.removeFromIniHint: Stops this mod loading by removing its workshop and mod IDs from the server INI. Keeps it in the panel's tracked list.
activeMods.removeFromServerHint: Stops this mod loading and removes it from the panel's tracked list. Workshop files remain on disk.
activeMods.missingRequiredTooltip: {{dep}} is not enabled — this mod may not work
activeMods.openWorkshopToChooseHint: Open the workshop page to see which mod ID(s) you should enable
activeMods.enabledOfTotalTooltip: {{enabled}} of {{total}} mod IDs enabled. Some workshop items ship multiple compatible IDs (e.g. add-on packs); others ship alternatives (e.g. Lite vs Full). Check the workshop page if unsure.
activeMods.chipTooltipClash: ⚠ Conflicts with {{names}} — both are enabled and share files. The one loaded last will overwrite the other.
activeMods.chipTooltipOverlap: Variant of {{names}} — these share files, so only one should be enabled at a time. Currently safe.
activeMods.clashWarning: Two variants of this mod are enabled and share files. One will overwrite the other — disable one.
activeMods.dismissOneTooltip: Mark "{{a}} ↔ {{b}}" as a false positive — useful when one ID is a shared library required by the other (e.g. a Common dependency).
activeMods.dismissAllTooltip: Mark all {{count}} flagged pairs in this workshop item as false positives.
activeMods.variantsShareFilesTooltip: These variants share files: {{ids}}. Enabling more than one would cause the last-loaded mod to overwrite the others. You currently have only one enabled — nothing to fix.
activeMods.variantsShareFiles: Variants share files — only one is enabled, which is the right setup.
activeMods.multipleEnabledHint: {{count}} mod IDs enabled. If unsure whether they coexist, check the workshop page.
activeMods.restoreDismissedTooltip_one: Restore {{count}} dismissed conflict pair for this workshop item
activeMods.restoreDismissedTooltip_other: Restore {{count}} dismissed conflict pairs for this workshop item
activeMods.nothingNeedsAttention: Nothing needs attention — no clashes, missing IDs, or duplicates.
activeMods.noMatchesFound: No matches found. Try the Steam search page if the dependency has a different Workshop title.
activeMods.pickMatchingItem: Pick the matching Workshop item, then add it to the server config.
activeMods.removeWorkshopDialogDesc: This will remove the workshop item and its mod IDs from the server INI. Workshop files on disk won't be deleted.

loadOrder.emptyDesc: Enable mods in the Active Mods tab first.
loadOrder.dragHint: Drag to reorder. Changes are not saved until you click Save.
loadOrder.basedOnDependencies_one: Based on {{count}} dependency declared in mod.info. Mods with no dependency keep your order.
loadOrder.basedOnDependencies_other: Based on {{count}} dependencies declared in mod.info. Mods with no dependency keep your order.
loadOrder.circularDependency: Circular dependency between {{mods}}. No order can satisfy it, so these keep their current order relative to each other.
loadOrder.missingRequirements_one: {{count}} required mod is not enabled and could not be ordered (see the Conflicts tab).
loadOrder.missingRequirements_other: {{count}} required mods are not enabled and could not be ordered (see the Conflicts tab).

addModsTab.syncDesc: Reads mod.info from downloaded mods and adds their IDs to Mods= in the INI
addModsTab.noModsPendingDesc: Use the Server Mods tab to find and add new workshop items, or click Sync to detect new downloads.

presetsTab.saveDialogDesc: Save the current mod configuration as a preset for easy switching later.
presetsTab.namePlaceholder: e.g., Vanilla+ Light, Hardcore, RP Server
presetsTab.willSave: This will save {{workshopCount}} workshop items and {{modCount}} mod IDs.
presetsTab.emptyDesc: Save your current mod configuration to create a preset
presetsTab.applyDialogDesc: This will replace your current mod configuration with {{count}} mods from this preset. Your existing Mods= and WorkshopItems= lines will be overwritten.
presetsTab.deleteDialogDesc: This preset will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be undone.

toolsTab.repairTooltip: Validate and remove invalid map entries
toolsTab.repairFailed: Map repair failed — check server connection
toolsTab.loadOrderMattersDesc: Frameworks and dependencies must load before content mods. Wrong order can cause silent failures.
toolsTab.mapModsCareDesc: After importing map mods, verify map folder names so spawns and cells load correctly.
toolsTab.syncAfterDownloadDesc: Workshop items without matching mod IDs usually means Steam hasn't finished downloading.

deactivatedTab.title: Deactivated Mods
deactivatedTab.description: Tracked by the panel but not present in the server INI's <1>WorkshopItems=</1> list. They won't be loaded by the server. Re-enable to put them back into the INI, or delete to stop tracking entirely.
deactivatedTab.emptyDesc: Every tracked mod is referenced in the server INI's WorkshopItems= list.
deactivatedTab.destructive: config only, files stay on disk
deactivatedTab.deleteHint: Delete only removes panel tracking. Workshop files stay on disk, but you will need to add the mod manually later.
deactivatedTab.deleteSelectedConfirm_one: Remove {{count}} selected deactivated mod from tracking? The workshop files stay on disk -- you can re-add it later.
deactivatedTab.deleteSelectedConfirm_other: Remove {{count}} selected deactivated mods from tracking? The workshop files stay on disk -- you can re-add them later.
deactivatedTab.deleteAllConfirm_one: Remove ALL {{count}} deactivated mod from tracking? The workshop files stay on disk -- you can re-add it later.
deactivatedTab.deleteAllConfirm_other: Remove ALL {{count}} deactivated mods from tracking? The workshop files stay on disk -- you can re-add them later.
deactivatedTab.genericNameNotice_one: <1>{{count}}</1> mod shows a generic name. Click <3>Refresh names</3> to look it up (checks disk first, then the Steam Workshop API).
deactivatedTab.genericNameNotice_other: <1>{{count}}</1> mods show a generic name. Click <3>Refresh names</3> to look them up (checks disk first, then the Steam Workshop API).

removeModDialog.title: Remove this mod from the server?
removeModDialog.description: This removes the mod from the server INI config so it stops loading. The Workshop files stay on disk (so re-adding later is instant).

bulkRemoveDialog.description: This removes the selected mods from the server INI config so they stop loading. Workshop files stay on disk (so re-adding later is instant).
